svg.aria-label: Claude Code, OpenAI Codex CLI and xAI Grok Build all run one Node script, handoff-guard.mjs, at their hook moments: it saves each chat’s recap as a note on disk, and asks git whether a 100% claim really changed its docs.
svg.text: One Node file runs at each tool’s hook moments and saves every chat’s recap for the next chat to pick up
Fires five hook events, plus a status line.
The baseline host. No host flag is needed.
Pass --host codex. The nudge reads token_count, and
with no status line, list shows the bars.
Fires seven, plus a status line you paste in.
Pass --host grok. The menu arrives with the first tool
result, and the status line caches the chat’s size.
Each chat’s recap is saved as JSON in its tool’s folder:
One note per chat. Kept 72 hours. This machine only.
When a recap claims 100%, git must show the docs it
If not, the reply is sent back with the reason, on every try.
No repository? Then there is nothing to check.
One Node file. Node built-ins only.
Each hook event runs one mode; Stop runs two. Every
mode exits 0, so a broken hook never blocks the tool.
A new chat is shown a menu of recent notes. Say “carry
on with …” and the model runs takeover for you.
Credential shapes are redacted before a note is written.
Other chats’ notes are shown to the model as data,
INSTALL, PROOF AND WHAT IT NEVER DOES
One installer per tool. Each is a dry run until you add --write, and it backs up
every file it changes. Node 20 or later.
75 tests and 103 mutations, all killed: run them before you install. CI on Ubuntu
No network, no telemetry, no dependencies. It never edits your code. It writes
only to its own handoff folder, and git is only read.
ai-session-handoff · one script, three tools · github.com/southlodge/ai-session-handoff
